title: Uhud — A Story of Patience and Obedience

lines.text: In the third year after the Hijrah, beneath a mountain north of Madinah, a small band of believers would face one of their hardest tests.
lines.say: In the third year after the Hijrah, beneath a mountain north of {madinah}, a small band of believers would face one of their hardest tests.

lines.text: This is the story of Uhud.
lines.say: This is the story of {uhud}.

scenes.caption: MAKKAH · 3 AH

lines.text: A year earlier, at Badr, the Quraysh of Makkah had suffered a defeat they could not forget.
lines.say: A year earlier, at {badr}, the {quraysh} of {makkah} had suffered a defeat they could not forget.

lines: Their leaders swore revenge, and poured the profits of an entire trade caravan into a new army.

lines.text: In the month of Shawwal, three thousand men marched north, with two hundred horses and seven hundred coats of armour.
lines.say: In the month of {shawwal}, three thousand men marched north, with two hundred horses and seven hundred coats of armour.

lines.text: Abu Sufyan led them. And on their right wing rode the cavalry of a brilliant young commander: Khalid ibn al-Walid.
lines.say: {abusufyan} led them. And on their right wing rode the cavalry of a brilliant young commander: {khalid}.

scenes.caption: MADINAH

lines.text: In Madinah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gathered his companions for counsel.
lines.say: In {madinah}, the Messenger of Allah, {saw}, gathered his companions for counsel.

lines: His own view was to defend the city from within its walls.

lines.text: But many young men, who had missed the battle of Badr, longed to meet the enemy in the open field.
lines.say: But many young men, who had missed the battle of {badr}, longed to meet the enemy in the open field.

lines.text: The Prophet ﷺ accepted the counsel of the majority, and put on his armour.
lines.say: The Prophet, {saw}, accepted the counsel of the majority, and put on his armour.

lines: About one thousand men set out.

lines.text: But on the way, Abdullah ibn Ubayy turned back with nearly three hundred of his followers.
lines.say: But on the way, {ibnubayy} turned back with nearly three hundred of his followers.

lines: Now only seven hundred remained, against an army more than four times their size.

lines.text: The Prophet ﷺ placed his army with Mount Uhud at its back.
lines.say: The Prophet, {saw}, placed his army with Mount {uhud} at its back.

lines: To one side rose a small hill. From there, enemy horsemen could sweep around behind the Muslim lines.

lines.text: So he posted fifty archers on that hill, under the command of Abdullah ibn Jubayr.
lines.say: So he posted fifty archers on that hill, under the command of {ibnjubayr}.

lines: His command to them was clear.
Even if you see birds snatching at us, do not leave your place until I send for you.
And even if you see us defeat them, do not leave your place until I send for you.

lines.text: One after another, the standard-bearers of Quraysh fell.
lines.say: One after another, the standard-bearers of {quraysh} fell.

lines: The arrows of the archers held the enemy cavalry back, and the Muslim ranks pressed forward.

lines.text: Among the bravest was Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib, the uncle of the Prophet ﷺ, known as the Lion of Allah.
lines.say: Among the bravest was {hamzah}, the uncle of the Prophet, {saw}, known as the Lion of Allah.

lines.text: But hidden among the rocks waited Wahshi, a slave who had been promised his freedom for the life of Hamzah.
lines.say: But hidden among the rocks waited {wahshi}, a slave who had been promised his freedom for the life of {hamza}.

lines: A single spear was thrown, and the Lion of Allah fell as a martyr.

lines.text: Soon the lines of Quraysh broke, and they fled, leaving their camp behind.
lines.say: Soon the lines of {quraysh} broke, and they fled, leaving their camp behind.

lines: On the hill, the archers saw the spoils of war in the valley below. The victory is won, some cried.

lines.text: Abdullah ibn Jubayr reminded them of the command of the Prophet ﷺ. But about forty of them went down.
lines.say: {ibnjubayr} reminded them of the command of the Prophet, {saw}. But about forty of them went down.

lines.text: Khalid ibn al-Walid had been waiting for exactly this moment.
lines.say: {khalid} had been waiting for exactly this moment.

lines: His horsemen rode around the hill, overwhelmed the few archers who remained, and struck the Muslims from behind.

lines.text: The fleeing Quraysh turned back. In moments, victory turned into chaos.
lines.say: The fleeing {quraysh} turned back. In moments, victory turned into chaos.

lines.text: Then a cry spread across the field, that Muhammad ﷺ had been killed.
lines.say: Then a cry spread across the field, that {muhammad_saw} had been killed.

lines.text: Many lost heart. But Anas ibn an-Nadr said: What will you do with life after him? Rise, and die for what he died for.
lines.say: Many lost heart. But {anas} said: What will you do with life after him? Rise, and die for what he died for.

lines.text: And he said: I can smell the fragrance of Paradise from beyond Uhud. He charged forward, and was martyred.
lines.say: And he said: I can smell the fragrance of Paradise from beyond {uhud}. He charged forward, and was martyred.

lines.text: In truth, the Prophet ﷺ was alive, though wounded.
lines.say: In truth, the Prophet, {saw}, was alive, though wounded.

lines.text: A small band of companions surrounded him, shielding him with their own bodies, among them a woman, Nusaybah bint Ka'b.
lines.say: A small band of companions surrounded him, shielding him with their own bodies, among them a woman, {nusaybah}.

lines.text: Slowly they climbed the slopes of Uhud, and the scattered believers gathered around him once more.
lines.say: Slowly they climbed the slopes of {uhud}, and the scattered believers gathered around him once more.

lines.text: From below, Abu Sufyan shouted: Exalted be Hubal!
lines.say: From below, {abusufyan} shouted: {ulhubal}! Exalted be Hubal!

lines.text: The Prophet ﷺ told his companions to answer: Allah is Most High and Most Majestic.
lines.say: The Prophet, {saw}, told his companions to answer: Allah is Most High and Most Majestic.

lines.text: Abu Sufyan called: We have al-Uzza, and you have no Uzza.
lines.say: {abusufyan} called: We have {uzza}, and you have no {uzza}.

lines: They answered: Allah is our Protector, and you have no protector.

lines.text: Then the army of Quraysh turned, and went home to Makkah.
lines.say: Then the army of {quraysh} turned, and went home to {makkah}.

lines.text: Seventy companions were martyred at Uhud.
lines.say: Seventy companions were martyred at {uhud}.

lines: They were buried where they fell, in the clothes they wore, two and three to a grave.

lines.text: And the Prophet ﷺ said: I will be a witness for these on the Day of Resurrection.
lines.say: And the Prophet, {saw}, said: I will be a witness for these on the Day of Resurrection.

lines.text: Uhud was not the defeat of a faith. It was a lesson, written in sacrifice.
lines.say: {uhud} was not the defeat of a faith. It was a lesson, written in sacrifice.

lines: Victory comes with obedience, and the love of this world can turn triumph into loss.
And Allah revealed: Do not weaken, and do not grieve, for you will be superior, if you are true believers.

lines.text: Surah Al 'Imran, 3:139
lines.say: Surah Al Imran, verse one hundred and thirty-nine.
